concepts.mechanism_summary: A ratchet consists of a round gear or linear rack with asymmetrical teeth, and a pivoting, spring-loaded finger called a pawl that engages the teeth. The teeth have a moderate slope on one edge and a much steeper slope on the other. When moving in the forward direction, the pawl slides up and over the gently sloped edges of the teeth, dropping into gaps with a click. When reversed, the pawl jams against the steep face of the nearest tooth, instantly preventing backward motion. This asymmetric geometry converts bidirectional applied force into net unidirectional motion. A small amount of backward travel ('backlash') occurs before the pawl re-engages the next steep face.

concepts.mechanism_summary: A differential gear is a gear arrangement that permits power from the engine to be transmitted to a pair of driving wheels, dividing force equally between them but allowing each to rotate at a different speed. Two bevel pinions (planet pinions) mesh with two bevel side gears, one on each axle. On a straight road, wheels turn at the same speed and the pinions rotate as a unit with the carrier/ring gear. In a turn, the outer wheel must travel farther; the side gears rotate relative to the pinions, allowing speed difference. The fundamental constraint is: angular velocity of left wheel + right wheel = 2 × carrier speed (the sum is constant).

atoms.verbatim_quote: A differential gear is a gear arrangement that permits power from the engine to be transmitted to a pair of driving wheels, dividing the force equally between them but permitting them to follow paths of different lengths
atoms.mechanism_atom: The differential distributes a fixed total torque between two outputs, allowing each to vary its speed independently while the sum (or torque ratio) remains constrained

atoms.verbatim_quote: For a symmetric bevel differential, the angular velocities satisfy ωL + ωR = 2ωC, reflecting that the carrier speed is the average of the side gear speeds
atoms.mechanism_atom: Planet-gear constraint enforces a linear speed-sum equation between two outputs, enabling one to compensate when the other is forced by external conditions

atoms.verbatim_quote: On a straight road the wheels and the side gears rotate at the same speed, there is no relative motion between the differential side gears and pinions, and they all rotate as a unit with the case and ring gear
atoms.mechanism_atom: Under uniform load, differential locks into synchronized rotation; asymmetric resistance (terrain/turn) automatically redistributes torque to the lower-resistance path

concepts.mechanism_summary: The Venturi effect describes the behavior of an incompressible fluid flowing through a constricted section of a pipe. As the fluid enters the narrow throat, mass continuity requires velocity to increase (A1v1 = A2v2). By Bernoulli's principle, the gain in kinetic energy is balanced by a drop in static pressure. Any gain in kinetic energy a fluid may attain by its increased velocity through a constriction is balanced by a drop in pressure because of its loss in potential energy. The low pressure at the throat can be used to entrain secondary fluids (ejectors, carburetors) or to measure flow rate (Venturi meter).

atoms.verbatim_quote: In inviscid fluid dynamics, an incompressible fluid's velocity must increase as it passes through a constriction in accord with the principle of mass continuity
atoms.mechanism_atom: Mass continuity forces velocity increase at a constriction, creating measurable acceleration proportional to cross-section reduction

atoms.verbatim_quote: Any gain in kinetic energy a fluid may attain by its increased velocity through a constriction is balanced by a drop in pressure because of its loss in potential energy
atoms.mechanism_atom: Bernoulli conservation trades potential energy (pressure) for kinetic energy (velocity) at the constriction — pressure drop is the measurable signal of flow acceleration

atoms.verbatim_quote: The reduction in pressure inside the constriction can be used both for measuring the fluid flow and for moving other fluids (e.g. in a vacuum ejector)
atoms.mechanism_atom: Throat pressure drop creates a suction that passively entrains secondary fluid without additional pumping — a constriction-induced pull mechanism

concepts.mechanism_summary: A siphon is an inverted U-shaped tube that moves liquid from a higher reservoir over a barrier and down into a lower reservoir, driven entirely by the head difference between the two free surfaces. Once primed (air evacuated from the tube), the siphon is self-sustaining: gravity pulling down the taller downward column creates reduced pressure at the crest, drawing fluid up from the upper reservoir without further energy input. The operation depends upon gravity, atmospheric pressure, and the cohesive forces that prevent the column of liquid from breaking. Flow stops only when the source reservoir drops below the tube inlet or the outlet rises above the source level. At sea level, water can be lifted a little more than 10 metres.

atoms.verbatim_quote: Once fluid has been forced over the highest point of a siphon, gravity pulling down the fluid on the longer side creates a vacuum that draws more fluid over the peak, initiating continuous flow
atoms.mechanism_atom: Post-prime self-sustaining flow: downstream gravitational pull continuously regenerates the pressure differential that drives fluid over the elevated barrier without ongoing external input

atoms.verbatim_quote: Priming arrangement is needed through either submerge-and-cap, mouth suction, or a squeeze bulb on the discharge end. Without complete air evacuation the column breaks at the crest
atoms.mechanism_atom: Priming (one-time initialization that evacuates air) is a prerequisite for flow onset — without it the barrier is insurmountable; once primed, no further initialization is needed

atoms.verbatim_quote: The outlet end must be lower than the source surface — that vertical difference is the head driving flow. Longer drop means higher velocity, capped by tube friction losses
atoms.mechanism_atom: Endpoint potential difference (elevation head) is the sole sustained driver of flow; the greater the height differential, the faster the self-sustaining transfer rate

concepts.mechanism_summary: Metathesis (from Greek 'to put in a different order') is a phonological process in which two or more sounds — consonants, vowels, or syllables — switch positions within a word or morpheme. Unlike deletion or insertion, metathesis preserves segment identity while altering their sequence. It can be triggered by perceptual salience (shifting a consonant from an obscured environment to one where its acoustic cues are clearer), syllable structure constraints (avoiding illegal clusters), or morphological marking. Adjacent (local) metathesis swaps contiguous sounds; non-adjacent (long-range) metathesis swaps sounds separated by intervening segments. It appears in child language acquisition, speech errors, diachronic change, and as a synchronic morphological alternation (e.g. Amarasi CV-metathesis).

atoms.verbatim_quote: Metathesis in linguistics refers to a phonological process in which two or more sounds, such as consonants or vowels, switch positions within a word, morpheme, or across linguistic contexts, resulting in a reversal of their original order
atoms.mechanism_atom: Segment transposition swaps the linear positions of two phonological units while preserving their intrinsic features — a positional rearrangement operator that changes sequence without changing elements

atoms.verbatim_quote: Metathesis can be achieved by shifting a consonant from an environment in which its acoustic cues are obscured to one in which the cues to its identification are more robust
atoms.mechanism_atom: Perception-driven reordering moves a segment to a position of higher acoustic salience — a local optimization that improves discriminability by changing position, not content

atoms.verbatim_quote: Synchronic vowel-consonant metathesis functions as a phonological strategy to avoid violation of syllable structure constraints and to optimize the sonority cline of heterosyllabic consonant clusters
atoms.mechanism_atom: Constraint-repair reordering: phonotactic violations are resolved not by deletion but by swapping segment positions to satisfy well-formedness constraints with minimal change

Closest tangential results: (a) energy-based latent traversal (gradient descent in potential landscape, but that requires continuous optimization, not primed passivity); (b) bootstrapped RL (uses estimates iteratively, not self-sustaining from endpoints); (c) LLM barrier constraints (stability limits, not flow through barriers).
